findings.detail: The catalogue anti-filler check is specified catalogue-wide while release is specified leaf-staged, and nothing scopes the check. §5.6: 'The mechanical gate rejects TODO, TBD, known generic filler ... repeated normalized fragment bodies, generic check IDs, and missing evidence targets', with '0 of 115 leaves meets this gate'; §13's gate step 3 restates that the specification gate 'rejects unresolved mechanism markers and forbidden catalogue filler'; the AT-SHAPE-6 row restates it per-leaf across all 115. But §12.3 step 4 says 'The other 114 leaves are not release-blocking for this release', §14 says 'Slice 14's horizontal authoring of the other 114 leaves is not release-blocking for this release', and §17.2 step 4 still requires 'npm test passes on the final source state, with the specification gate ordered first'. Since AT-GATE-2's mechanism makes the specification gate the first element of npm test and short-circuits everything after it, 114 leaves holding TODO(Slice 10) fragments keep npm test permanently red, so the D21 lint-format release is unreachable by this document's own release gate. Either the filler check is scoped to production-supported leaves (never stated) or D21's narrowing is inoperative; Gate 2 prescribes both.

v0.7's grade-aware CI applicability contradicts Gate 1 AT-CI-3 and its own traceability row. §8.9: 'lint-format is repo-CI-applicable only at the Evidence grade (§11.3), so a lint-format leaf selected at Policy or Context grade does not run in this job and acquires no CI enforcement, even when another control or service caused a Rig CI job to exist.' Gate 1 AT-CI-3 requires that an integrated or bootstrapped pipeline 'runs all enabled baseline controls and selected executable services', and the §13 AT-CI-3 row restates it unnarrowed as 'CI runs all enabled repo controls/services'. A Policy-grade lint-format leaf is a selected executable service (AD-32: 'The disposition is executable'), so on one fixture — Rig CI job present, lint-format selected at Policy — the AT-CI-3 test must assert the service runs and the AT-LF-13 test must assert it does not. Gate 1's AT-LF-13 conditions only the CI graft on the Evidence level; it never authorizes excluding lower grades from an existing job, so this exclusion is a Gate-2 invention that overrides a frozen Gate-1 clause.

Whether the CI gate is a constituent of the Evidence grade is prescribed both ways. §5.7 makes it unconditional — 'Evidence runs every Context check plus its evidence work and §11.3 CI gate' — and adds 'never report assurance above the highest grade actually completed'. §11.3 makes it conditional — "'absent' or 'unsupported' CI gets nothing written until the user selects one of the six providers (§11.2) and approves a separate plan" — and 'Selecting the Evidence grade proposes this gate; it never auto-creates or owns CI on selection alone.' Failure scenario: a repository with no CI, user selects Evidence and approves the plan, checks run and produce verifiable evidence. Under §5.7 a constituent of Evidence never ran, so reporting 'Evidence' over-claims assurance; reporting 'Context' instead means AT-LF-9's Evidence verdict is unreachable on any repository without CI. No clause resolves which, and §13's AT-LF-9 row omits CI entirely, so the test written from the row cannot detect either error.

The gate's existence check is vacuous for most rows. §13 requires that 'Every row must name an existing design anchor and a substantive executable test title containing the same ID' and that 'The gate stats every target named in the table and fails on absence'; §17.1 blocker 1 requires 'every row names a real design anchor and a substantive executable target'. In fact only AT-GATE-1 ('advanced-spec-gate.test.js') and the nineteen AT-LF-* rows name a target; the other 48 rows — including AT-GATE-2, AT-GATE-3, AT-SHAPE-1 through AT-SHAPE-6, AT-BASE-1 through AT-BASE-7, AT-B1 through AT-B7, AT-HOST-1/2/5, AT-CI-1 through AT-CI-4, AT-CLAIM-1, AT-PRESENCE-1/2, AT-HOME-1/2, AT-DIST-1, AT-INSTALL-1, AT-UNINSTALL-1/2/3, AT-REPORT-1, AT-SECRET-1 — carry only prose assertions with no file and no test title containing the ID. For those rows the stat-every-target check has nothing to stat and passes without evidence, which is precisely the 'node --test <missing-file> exits 0' failure §13 exists to close; and the document cannot satisfy its own freeze blocker 1.

Remediation is told to use a rollback path this document abolished, and its interaction with the install journal is unspecified. §8.7: remediation apply 'rechecks all preimages, rejects stale or empty/no-op work, uses the normal exclusive transaction/rollback path'; §10 and AD-8 repeat 'rollback'. But AD-10 states 'A failed apply never rolls back', §6.6 repeats it, and §2.1 lists 'Transactional rollback on a failed apply' as rejected, calling its earlier appearance in §6.6/§10 'an unreconciled leftover'. Gate 1 AT-B6 does require 'partial failure rolls back' for remediation, so the two behaviors must be separated explicitly — and §7.6 says the manifest covers 'every mutation Rig makes'. Failure scenario: remediation writes two files (journaled pending then applied with post-write digests), the third write fails, rollback reverts the first two. The manifest now holds 'applied' records for files that no longer match their recorded digests, so §7.6's resume ('Each applied record is verified against its recorded digest and skipped') blocks under the conflicting/unknown class, and uninstall's preimage diff reports best-effort on files that were correctly reverted. Neither §7.6 nor §8.7 says whether rolled-back writes are journaled, superseded, or excluded.

findings.anchor: §8.4 signer setup step 2 vs §1 (D20 paragraph) and §13 AT-PRESENCE-2 row
findings.detail: The single mechanism carrying AT-PRESENCE-2's live-human-act floor is stated unconditionally in two places and conditionally in the one place that specifies it. §1: 'What makes this hold rather than the label is the registration ceremony (§8.4): each recovery key is generated through a user-verification authenticator act, so an agent cannot register a key it could later operate unattended.' The §13 AT-PRESENCE-2 row asserts as testable that 'registration requires the user-verification ceremony'. §8.4 step 2 hedges: 'Rig invokes the platform OpenSSH ssh-keygen security-key flow for a sk-* key with user verification required where OpenSSH exposes it.' Failure scenario: on a platform whose OpenSSH does not expose the user-verification option, an agent holding a valid credential registers a resident sk-* key it can drive without a human, and Gate 2 specifies no behavior — no refusal, no disclosure difference, no degraded state — so the self-appointment AT-PRESENCE-2 exists to forbid succeeds while the declared class still reads sk-*. The test written from the row fails on that platform for a reason the design never resolves.

§9.3 states the on-disk enum as closed — 'Run-report status values written to disk are failed, vacuous, and coverage_gap' — while §9.4 requires six more: 'timeout, cancelled, missing_dependency, signalled, partial_output, and command_not_found', reconciled only by the sentence 'These extend the executable runner's §9.2/§9.3 run-report status set.' §9.3 itself, the report shape it prints, and the source-owned catalog/baseline/report-schema.json named in §4.1 are never restated with the extended set. An implementer building the report validator from §9.3, as §10's 'Reports | schema-validated' instructs, rejects all six and collapses them into failed — exactly what AT-LF-16 says fails the case.

A v0.7 document repeatedly speaks as v0.5, which matters because §17.1 is the freeze-blocker list a gate or reviewer reads to decide whether this file may be marked FROZEN. §17.1: 'Version 0.5 remains a candidate until all of the following hold.' §11.1: 'As of this v0.5 candidate, no host axis holds a complete emitted bundle.' §3: 'Blocking gaps still open at the last audit and still unresolved as work begins under v0.5'. As written, §17.1's conditions are scoped to a superseded version — the header states v0.7 'supersedes v0.6, and v0.5 before it, in full' — leaving no clause that names v0.7's own freeze conditions.
